plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: A fragrant evergreen shrub with silvery-gray foliage and slender spikes of small tubular flowers. Widely cultivated in gardens and commercial fields, it attracts bees and butterflies and is prized for its essential oil.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-June to August in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to the Mediterranean; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, Tasmania, and the northern United States
plants.funFact: Lavender was used by ancient Romans to scent their baths, and its name likely derives from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'.

plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with a large composite flower head made up of yellow ray florets surrounding a dark disk of tiny florets that mature into seeds. Young flower heads track the sun across the sky.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to North America; widely cultivated in Ukraine, Russia, Argentina, France, and the United States
plants.funFact: The flower head is actually made up of up to 2,000 individual tiny flowers, and the florets are arranged in spiral patterns following the Fibonacci sequence.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial with large round leaves held above the water and spectacular, fragrant flowers on tall stalks. Its leaves have a micro-textured surface that repels water and dirt.
plants.bloomingSeason: July to September in temperate Asia
plants.location: Native to Asia and Australia; found in ponds and wetlands in India, China, Japan, Vietnam, and cultivated worldwide
plants.funFact: Lotus seeds can remain viable for centuries; one seed about 1,300 years old was successfully germinated, and the flower is able to regulate its own temperature.

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: A hardy perennial prairie wildflower with daisy-like flowers with drooping petals around a spiky, orange-brown central cone. It is a favorite of pollinators and goldfinches, which eat the seeds in late summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: June to October in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to eastern and central North America; common in prairies, open woodlands, and cultivated gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Echinacea gets its name from the Greek 'echinos' meaning hedgehog, referring to the prickly central cone, and it has long been used in traditional Native American medicine.
